format.sourceSnippet: 19 What is the format or language of the interviews? Bilingual small group or individual interviews are usually scheduled. Details such as the date, time, and language of the interview will be provided in the interview invitation.

prepAdvice.sourceSnippet: Tips: Prepare the information in point form so you can easily present yourself no matter how you are being asked. Try NOT to recite the materials.

Research Visit the programme & university website Search if there are any latest developments in the programme / subject / discipline Reach out to your teachers & alumni for insights & advice Pay attention to local and international news

records.subject: Medicine (Med-P Qualifying Year leading to MDCM)

format.sourceSnippet: The interviews are in virtual multiple mini-interview (vMMI) format and are conducted virtually by the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences. These mini-interviews consist of multiple stations that can be task-oriented, simulation-oriented, scenario-oriented, or discussion-oriented.

numberAndLength.sourceSnippet: The virtual MMI is divided into 2 separate Zoom meetings, with a break in between. The length of each zoom interview session is up to one hour.

mmiStations.sourceSnippet: The M³I consists of a circuit of between 7 to 10 stations, which can be in any of the following formats: (a) discussion-based (with evaluator present) (b) task-oriented (with or without evaluator present) or (c) controlled scenarios or simulations (with evaluator observing from outside the room). Stations are 7 minutes long, (with the exception of 1 station whose duration is double the length).

whatIsAssessed.sourceSnippet: Stations are designed to evaluate the various non-medical abilities targeted in the MDCM Program Learning Objectives which in turn references the CanMeds roles developped by the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada. The MMIs can at times include themes that may be sensitive or personal for some candidates. Clinical skills are not tested.

prepAdvice.sourceSnippet: Preparation for the MMIs. It is unnecessary to pay for expensive training programs. We encourage you to be confident, and be yourself!
A s with all interviews, you are encouraged to reflect on your skills and strengths. Consider resources like your university or community career centre to learn more about the MMI format.

records.notes: The direct-entry route for this course is the Med-P Qualifying Year; Med-P page: 'This one-year Qualifying Year is designed exclusively for CEGEP students' (Quebec Collegial/DEC graduates). MMI page: 'Candidates cannot be admitted without an interview.' Application-process page lists Med-P interview dates 'April 20, 21, 22, 23, 2027' under '*(Interviews are held virtually)'. The MDCM itself (university-level entry) is not a high-school route. The older Med-P PDF (Fall 2021) describing in-person interviews was not used.

sampleQuestions.subject: Engineering
sampleQuestions.question: What experience(s), inside or outside the classroom, motivated you to apply to your chosen engineering program?
sampleQuestions.sourceSnippet: You will be asked to record a video response to the following question: What experience(s), inside or outside the classroom, motivated you to apply to your chosen engineering program?

prepAdvice.sourceSnippet: You will not be asked any skill-testing or technical questions, nor will you be required to solve engineering or technical problems. Instead, the questions will be interview-style, giving you an opportunity to demonstrate how you think, communicate, reflect and respond to different situations.

Structure your responses. Consider using a framework such as the S.T.A.R. method (Situation, Task, Action, Result) to organize your thoughts and communicate your experiences clearly. Practice speaking out loud.
You don’t need to memorize answers or try to present yourself in a certain way – just be yourself.

records.subject: Computer Science

format.sourceSnippet: The NUS Computing Aptitude-Based Admissions (ABA) scheme may include various processes, such as tests or individual or group interviews, depending on the specific department’s requirements.

prepAdvice.sourceSnippet: The ABA interviews are designed to assess candidates in various ways, and each interviewer may pose different questions. The purpose of the interview is for you to showcase your strengths and convince us why you are an ideal candidate for our programmes. Consider what makes you stand out, how best to articulate those qualities, and provide evidence to support your claims. In essence, be yourself, be compelling, and demonstrate why you are remarkable.

records.subject: Medicine (LKCMedicine MBBS)

format.sourceSnippet: This is conducted in eight (8) separate interview booths by faculty members, and professionals from various healthcare disciplines.

numberAndLength.sourceSnippet: The MMI typically takes place at the Novena campus in Singapore. Shortlisted applicants will complete the physical MMI on the day itself, usually within two hours.

mmiStations.sourceSnippet: Shortlisted applicants invited for the MMI will complete a series of eight (8) one-to-one interviews.

whatIsAssessed.sourceSnippet: They are a series of interviews designed to evaluate the applicant’s aptitude and capability to successfully complete the MBBS programme. This includes one’s motivation and realistic approach to medicine as a career, capacity to deal with stress, evidence of leadership and team participation, ability to multi-task, communication skills, maturity of character, and likely contribution to medical school life.

prepAdvice.sourceSnippet: LKCMedicine does not recommend any preparatory course for the MMI. Like many other interviews, just be yourself. Be calm and listen carefully to the questions asked by the interviewers.

records.notes: No applicant group is singled out on the LKCMedicine FAQ; it also states priority for admission is given to Singaporeans (not quoted here).

records.subject: Computer Science, Economics, Mechanical Engineering, Accounting & Finance
records.interviewed: some applicants (those studying certain qualifications, e.g. Access to HE Diploma or T Level); very exceptionally others

format.sourceSnippet: Interviews take place virtually via Microsoft Teams.

whatIsAssessed.sourceSnippet: The interview process is used to determine your suitability for the course you have applied for and to provide you with an opportunity to decide if our course is the right one for you.

prepAdvice.sourceSnippet: Think about what has motivated you to study the course and why you would like to study at the University of Bath Carefully consider what has really interested you during your current study and prepare some well thought out examples - which will help you evidence your enthusiasm and passion for your subject

Familiarise yourself with the published course material and look at which modules may be of interest to you Be prepared to discuss anything you have included in your personal statement and expand on this during your interview

You will also be asked to answer some academic subject-specific questions relating to your course. Please do not get anxious if you are unsure of the answer straight away; you will be given time to work through the question and the Admissions Tutor will support you and want to see how you can apply your logic to work out the answer.

records.notes: Each 2027 course page ("Selection process") says: "We will usually assess you based on your UCAS application." followed by the qualification sentence, e.g. Computer Science: "If you are studying certain qualifications, such as an Access to HE or T Level, you will be invited to attend an interview as part of our selection process." (Economics and Mechanical Engineering name the Access to HE Diploma; Accounting & Finance names Access to HE Diploma or T Level), and all add "Very exceptionally we may invite you to an interview if you have circumstances we cannot assess from an application alone." The interview guide (https://www.bath.ac.uk/guides/undergraduate-applicant-interviews/) adds: "Typically you will be interviewed by two or three members of staff including the Admissions Tutor and a member of our Undergraduate Progression Team." No length or sample questions published.
